outside $|z|<1$ or across a continuation cut is implicit.

finite_smoke.asserts: 1.2 The two series for $e^{-iz}$ and $e^{iz}$ are absolutely convergent by [F2], so [F7] identifies their product with the sum of the Cauchy-product coefficients. For total degree $n$, its coefficient is $z^n S_n$, where $S_n=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-i)^r i^{n-r}/(r!(n-r)!)$. For $1\le r\le n$, combining over the denominator $r!(n+1-r)!$ and using $(n+1-r)!=(n+1-r)(n-r)!$ and $r!=r(r-1)!$ gives $1/(r!(n+1-r)!)=(1/(n+1))(1/(r!(n-r)!)+1/((r-1)!(n+1-r)!))$. For $r=0$ or $r=n+1$, omit the summand whose index is outside $0,\ldots,n$; the remaining summand equals the left side by $0!=1$. Splitting the finite sum for $S_{n+1}$ with this identity and reindexing its second part gives $S_{n+1}=(iS_n-iS_n)/(n+1)=0$ for every $n\ge0$, while $S_0=1$. The factorials and $n+1$ are nonzero by [F2], so these divisions are defined. Hence the product series has constant coefficient $1$ and every positive-degree coefficient $0$, so $e^{-iz}e^{iz}=1$.
